kevin (ACME): Hey team — after we rotated our Redwood API key yesterday, our AWS Lambda-backed webhook started getting 401s. Thought it would pick up the new ENV var via deployment, but logs show old key being used. Any ideas?

Maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this, Kevin. Quick q: did you rotate via the Redwood Console or the API? And are you storing the key in plain Lambda env var or pulling from Secrets Manager / KMS?

kevin (ACME): Console. We updated the env var in our CI to the new key and pushed a new deployment, but the function still shows requests failing. We also see `401 invalid_api_key` from Redwood when invoking from lambda.

aj (support-engineer): Thanks — can you paste the exact error snippet (sanitized) and a small curl test from your box against the same key? Also, is your Lambda reading the key from an encrypted env var (KMS) or from plain text?

kevin (ACME): Error: `{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found or revoked"}`. From our staging box `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer NEWKEY123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines` returns 200. From inside lambda we see header `Authorization: Bearer OLDKEY456`. So the function runtime still has the old value.

Maya (support): OK that implies the deployment didn't roll the runtime that the live invocations are hitting. Two quick checks: 1) Did you update the env via console or via an infrastructure tool (CFN/SAM/Serverless)? 2) Any provisioned concurrency or long-running containers?

kevin (ACME): Serverless framework + provisioned concurrency enabled. We updated env in CI that triggers a deploy, but provisioned concurrency seemed to stay at the previous value.

aj (support-engineer): Provisioned concurrency keeps warm execution environments, they don't pick up env var changes until reprovisioned. If you update environment without updating the alias/config that backs provisioned concurrency, the warm pools will keep the old env. You need to redeploy/reprovision or bump the provisioned concurrency to force a replacement.

Devon (eng-infra): Adding — another common issue: if your Lambda decrypts the value at start using a KMS CMK, the function's execution role needs kms:Decrypt permission on the CMK. If you rotated the key object in Secrets Manager (which rewraps with a new CMK) and the role lacks access, the cold start can fallback to cached secret (old). Check CloudWatch startup logs for KMS decryption errors.

kevin (ACME): Hmm our role recently had a least-priv change; possible. I do see some `AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key` in CloudWatch around the rotation time. So lambda might have failed to decrypt and kept older cached secret in memory.

Maya (support): That lines up. Two remediation paths: 1) Fix the IAM/CMS policy so the Lambda execution role can kms:Decrypt on the new CMK and then redeploy/recycle provisioned concurrency. 2) As a fast temporary workaround, create a short-lived API key in Redwood and update your deployment to use that (then rotate when stable).

kevin (ACME): Can you confirm the exact aws cli command to force a redeploy that will refresh provisioned concurrency? We're using serverless framework so don't want to do something unsafe.

aj (support-engineer): For Serverless you can bump a config value or run `aws lambda update-function-configuration --function-name my-fn --environment "Variables={REDWOOD_API_KEY=NEWVALUE}"` which will create a new function configuration and cause new warmers to be provisioned. To specifically update provisioned concurrency: `aws lambda put-provisioned-concurrency-config --function-name my-fn --qualifier prod --provisioned-concurrent-executions 5` (adjust as needed). Alternatively in Serverless, update the alias hash so provisioned concurrency is redeployed.

kevin (ACME): Trying the `update-function-configuration` now. Also fixing IAM to add kms:Decrypt to the execution role.

ops-bot: Notice — function my-fn (prod) invoked 1200 times in last 10m, AVG duration 320ms, provisioned concurrency 5 (stable).

kevin (ACME): After `update-function-configuration` runs, CW shows new config version and CloudWatch logs show cold start with `Decrypt succeeded`. Invocations now send NEWKEY123. No more 401s. Thanks.

Devon (eng-infra): FYI: Longer-term we recommend using Secrets Manager with an explicit rotation lambda or using the Redwood dedicated key rotation webhook, and make sure your deployment pipeline updates alias/config that your provisioned concurrency points at. Also, add a startup health check that logs env hash so you can detect stale env usage quickly.

Sara (security): A couple security notes: 1) Don't store long-lived plaintext API keys in public repos. 2) If you rotate keys, consider short TTLs for the keys used by ephemeral compute or use IAM-backed role auth where possible. 3) We should audit CMK policies to ensure cross-account principals aren't overexposed.

kevin (ACME): Agreed — we'll move to Secrets Manager with rotation. One quick ask: can Redwood provide a webhook we can call from our rotation lambda to programmatically create/retire keys and validate they work?

Maya (support): Yes — Redwood has an API for key creation/rotation. I'll DM the dev docs link and open a ticket to get you a sample rotation lambda (we have a reference for AWS Secrets Manager that calls Redwood's rotate endpoint and runs a smoke curl).

aj (support-engineer): I'll attach the quick smoke test here for your rotation lambda — run this after updating secret to verify key works before switching traffic:

```bash
# quick smoke test (from the rotation lambda)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANDIDATE_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .status
# expect: {"status":"ok"}
```

kevin (ACME): Dropping this in our rotation job. Big thanks. Last question: does Redwood offer short-lived ephemeral keys for functions so we can avoid long-lived keys in envs?

Maya (support): We offer scoped API tokens and a rotate endpoint; short-lived tokens are on the roadmap. I'll flag this feature request to product and link you to the internal ticket.

kevin (ACME): Perfect. Closing this out on our side — resolved after IAM fix + forced redeploy. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
